verdict.rationale: CodeRabbit runs on its own in the background. It reviews pull requests automatically once they open, configured through `reviews.auto_review` (branches, labels, drafts, pausing). It also analyzes CI/CD failures without being asked and can deliver the Triage queue as a scheduled digest. These are fixed, review-centric triggers rather than general automations a user defines; custom recipes are one-click actions, not background jobs. Missing for 10: a user-defined automation builder (custom triggers and actions), recurring scheduled agent tasks beyond the Triage digest, and independent hands-on corroboration of background autonomy.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Configure when and how CodeRabbit automatically reviews pull requests using the `reviews.auto_review` settings.
you can disable reviews globally and re-enable them by keyword or label, apply them only to certain branches, skip draft PRs, and pause after a set number of commits
When a CI/CD pipeline fails on a pull request, CodeRabbit reads the failure output and posts inline comments with suggested fixes
Get your Triage queue as a scheduled digest
